scope: Isolated synthetic fixture + isolated server copies only; no production data, no production calls.

Submenu opens (existing behaviour) and its items stay readable
Navigation clicks still switch sections exactly as before
Mobile drawer renders the same surface with all menu rows

B1 Deleting a live number removes its Test Panel twin (single delete)
B2 Test Panel list no longer returns the orphan
C1 Deleting via "delete filtered" also clears the Test Panel twin
D1 Deleting a whole range clears matching test entries, keeps the others
E1 Moving a test number back creates an unallocated live number in its range
E2 Moved number is visible in the live Numbers list
E3 Moving again is refused (no duplicate live row, pool row kept)
F1 Bulk delete removes exactly the selected rows and refreshes mirrors
F2 Range-wise delete clears the whole range list and the mirror
G1 Non-admin roles cannot delete or move Test Panel numbers
G2 Existing single delete route still works
G3 Bad input is rejected without side effects
H0 A live number is still available for the SMS regression probes
H1 Same provider id delivered 3× still stores exactly one row

sms_ingestion_regression: same provider id delivered repeatedly → one stored row (dedup ledger)
identical text with no provider id → stored (never treated as a duplicate)
legitimate resend 1 s later with a new event id → separate row
same CLI+number with a different OTP → separate row
unknown number → HTTP 404 + failed_sms_queue entry, nothing stored
two server processes receiving the same provider id simultaneously → one stored row

high_rate_measurement.isolated_config: API_RATE_PER_MIN raised only on the throwaway audit instance for the measurement; production/default 1200 per minute restored afterwards and unchanged in the source.

known_limitations: The callback channel identifies a message by the provider message id only; when a provider sends no id, identical text is stored again (by design, so genuine resends are never lost).
The SMPP path uses a 10-second fingerprint bucket when the peer supplies no receipted message id; a retransmission inside that window is suppressed, one after it is stored again.
api_integration_seen keeps the newest ~50,000 provider ids (default); older ids are pruned, so a very late retransmission of a pruned id is stored again.
smpp_seen rows are cleared when the SMPP connection record is deleted, so identity history restarts if a connection is recreated.
